issue: Does Kisor v. Wilkie's limit on Auer/Seminole Rock deference apply to the Sentencing Guidelines commentary, so that a court may defer to the commentary only if the Guideline itself is genuinely ambiguous?
provision: U.S.S.G. commentary (Stinson v. United States, 508 U.S. 36 (1993); Kisor v. Wilkie, 139 S. Ct. 2400 (2019))

sides.position: Kisor's more demanding deference standard applies to Guidelines commentary; a court may defer to commentary only if the Guideline is genuinely ambiguous after exhausting traditional tools of construction.
cases: United States v. Riccardi, 989 F.3d 476 (6th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Castillo, 69 F.4th 648 (9th Cir. 2023)
United States v. Scheu, No. 22-10044 (9th Cir. 2023)

sides.position: Kisor did not displace Stinson; the Guidelines commentary continues to receive deference under Stinson without first requiring a finding of ambiguity in the Guideline.
cases: United States v. Moses, 23 F.4th 347 (4th Cir. 2022)

this_court: Follows the Kisor-applies position (adopted in Castillo, which Scheu reaffirms). Scheu itself does not decide the broader post-Kisor question of how much weight commentary receives, because it holds the Guideline unambiguous.
quote: Since Kisor was decided, a circuit split has arisen over whether this more limited deference should apply to the Sentencing Guidelines commentary and application notes.
cite: United States v. Joshua Scheu, No. 22-10044 (9th Cir. 2023)
